h1: # The Uniontown Hospital Vape Alarm (early April 2018)
body:
During the four-day death watch at Uniontown Hospital, in the pediatric wing
where [[wiki/people/fran-coldren|Fran Coldren]] was dying of a deliberate
water shutdown, Dan Frank stepped into the room's bathroom, took one pull
from a high-wattage sub-ohm vaporizer, set off the smoke detector, and
triggered a fire alarm that chain-spread across the entire hospital. Four
fire trucks arrived within minutes. Firefighters and a security guard
entered the room; Dan told them the device "went off in my pocket"; they
shook their heads, killed the alarms, and walked him off the property, where
the guard wrote up charging documents. Those documents were real: a summary
non-traffic case was filed with the Fayette County magistrate on **April 5,
2018**, the day after Fran died, under docket **MJ-14101-NT-0000082-2018**, on a
single charge of *smoking* in a hospital. It is the corpus's second documented
brush with charges, and by some distance its most disproportionate: the thing
obtained was one drag of nicotine.

This page exists partly to close a gap. The Photo Thread session that
supplied most of [[wiki/timeline/events/fran-death-vigil]] set this story up
— the enormous SMOK box mod against [[wiki/people/suzanne-frank|Suz's]]
dainty 10-watt eJoy — and then delivered the ending only inside an uploaded
video that is not on disk. The vigil page has carried "fire alarm? staff
incident?" as an open question since 2026-07-19. It was a fire alarm.

## The reasoning, which is the actual content

What distinguishes this from an ordinary lapse is that it was not one. Dan's
account is emphatic that he ran the argument first and found it sound:
smoke detectors respond to *combustion* particulates; a vaporizer does not
burn anything; the two aerosols look alike but are physically different; the
detector, correctly understood, would agree with him. He describes himself
in that moment by the subculture's own title — "it's 2018, I'm a fucking
cloud king" — and notes that cloud kings are not stupid. The deduction is
valid in form and false in its premise, which is precisely the shape
[[wiki/mind/profile/big-five-psychometrics]] describes as the
intellect/impulsivity paradox: top-percentile reasoning recruited *to
authorize* an impulse rather than to interrogate it. The reasoning did not
slow the urge down. It cleared it for takeoff.

His account of the aftermath is timed to the second and worth keeping in his
proportions: five seconds to understand what had happened, one second to
grasp the magnitude — the coming embarrassment, the "bone shaking stupidity
of the act itself," and the absurdity of setting off a mass emergency
response while his great-grandmother, so dehydrated she looked like a
skeleton, lay dying in the middle of the room. He then sat down on the couch
next to [[wiki/people/annie-ulmer|Annie]], who had no idea what had
happened, and said nothing at all until the firefighters walked in.

## The priming

Dan attributes the act, hedged, to something he had watched a few hours
earlier: Suz standing in the hospital room taking small drags from a tiny
eJoy vape, "just not even spoken of, it happens so naturally." His own
gloss — "this action must have absorbed into my subconscious somehow" — is
the only causal account anyone has offered, and it is worth taking
seriously in the specific form he gives it. What transferred was not the
idea of vaping; it was the observation that nobody had objected. The
family's characteristic move of normalizing the unremarkable-in-context is,
here, the thing that produced a consequence.

> **CONTRADICTION [2026-08-02] — who was where.**
> [[wiki/timeline/events/fran-death-vigil]], written from the Photo Thread
> session, has Dan blowing enormous clouds from a 110-watt SMOK **in the
> room** while Suz puffed her 10-watt device **in the hospital bathroom**.
> Both captures behind this page invert that: **Suz in the room, Dan in the
> bathroom.** The positions are not decorative — a bathroom smoke detector is
> exactly where an alarm would trip, so the capture's arrangement is the one
> that produces the documented outcome, while the vigil's arrangement does
> not obviously produce it at all. Neither account is contemporaneous and
> both are Dan's, roughly two weeks apart. Recorded here unresolved; if the
> `IMG_`-series uploads are ever recovered, they settle it.

## The legal residue — a filed summary case, docket MJ-14101-NT-0000082-2018

> **GAP CLOSED [2026-08-22]:** This page asked, from its creation until now,
> *"Whether a summary offense was actually filed with a Fayette County
> magistrate, or whether the paperwork was an incident report a security guard
> described in charging language, is unestablished and answerable only from
> outside the corpus."* It was filed. The operator supplied the summons
> (`raw/legal/documents/2018-04_summons-hospital-smoking.md`): a
> **Summons for Summary Case — Non-Traffic**, *Commonwealth of Pennsylvania v.
> Daniel G Frank*, docket **MJ-14101-NT-0000082-2018**, citation **R 2009305-4**,
> **case filed 4/5/2018** before **Magisterial District Judge Michael M. Metros**,
> MDJ-14-1-01, 88 North Gallatin Avenue, Uniontown. The security guard's
> "charging documents" were charging documents.

| field | value |
|---|---|
| Docket | MJ-14101-NT-0000082-2018 |
| Citation | R 2009305-4 |
| Case filed | 2018-04-05 |
| Summons printed | 2018-04-05, 2:51:15 PM |
| Court | MDJ-14-1-01, Hon. Michael M. Metros, 88 N. Gallatin Ave, Uniontown PA |
| Defendant address of record | 337 Saratoga Dr, Uniontown PA 15401 |
| Charge (sole, lead) | LO § 1639 §§ b 1 — "Smoking prohibited w/in certain public premises including hospital properties" |
| Fine and costs | printed on the sheet, not legible in the surviving frames |
| Plea stub | undetached, both signature lines blank |
| Document photographed | 2018-04-17, 4:31 PM and 4:41 PM, Uniontown |

**The charge is smoking.** One count, marked `(Lead)` with nothing under it — a
local ordinance violation, the smallest instrument the Commonwealth had
available. Four fire trucks turned out, an alarm chain-spread through an entire
hospital, and no one filed for causing a false alarm (18 Pa.C.S. § 4905),
disorderly conduct, criminal mischief or trespass. This cuts against the
disproportion reading the page has carried, and it is worth being precise about
which direction: the paperwork is grotesquely out of proportion to *one drag of
nicotine*, and simultaneously far *under* proportion to the emergency response it
caused. Fayette County priced the incident as a smoking violation. That is a
narrower answer than either "nothing happened" or "he was charged for the alarm,"
and it is the one on the docket.

There is a second thing the charge does, which the reasoning section above sets
up without knowing it. Dan's entire argument was that **a vaporizer does not
burn anything** — no combustion, no smoke, therefore no detector and no
offence. The charge the Commonwealth filed is *smoking*, at a hospital, under an
ordinance written for cigarettes. The citation does not engage his distinction;
it declines it. The one document in the record that responds to the cloud king's
deduction responds by categorising the act as the thing he had proved it was not.

**The response is not recorded.** Both plea lines are blank and the stub is
undetached in a photograph taken twelve days after the summons was printed —
which is past the ten-day window the form specifies, though the receipt date
rather than the print date starts that clock and the receipt date is unknown.
Whether Dan pleaded, paid, appeared, or let it run to the arrest warrant the
form threatens is unestablished; nothing in eleven years of message record
mentions a court date, a fine, or this docket. The Pennsylvania UJS web portal
the summons itself names would settle it in one lookup, from outside the corpus.

**The address is the second document.** The summons gives the defendant's
address as **337 Saratoga Dr, Uniontown PA 15401**, printed April 5, 2018 —
and that is a fact about where Dan lived, filed by a court, in a period the
wiki has been reconstructing entirely from testimony and message metadata.
[[wiki/places/155-virginia-ave|155 Virginia Avenue]] is where the residence
timeline puts him from January 2015 to February 2019, and that page carries an
**eviction notice served on him at 155 Virginia on March 29, 2018** — mid-vigil,
by [[wiki/people/diane-moore|Dian V. Moore]], demanding the keys — whose outcome
it records as undocumented. It is documented now, and by an accident: seven days
after the notice, the address the Commonwealth had for him was his mother's
house. [[wiki/places/117-belmont-circle]] reached the same conclusion from the
other side, observing that through spring 2018 he "had somewhere else to be";
this names which somewhere, on a dated official record, and it is
[[wiki/places/337-saratoga-drive|337 Saratoga]] rather than Belmont Circle.

The caution that keeps this from being more than it is: a summons address is
whatever address the citing officer or the court had, which may be a
driver's-licence address rather than a place of sleep, and the two need not
agree. It establishes that 337 Saratoga was Dan's address **of record** in April
2018. It does not establish that he was sleeping there, and the Belmont Circle
evidence has him using a third house across the same months. What it removes is
the possibility that 155 Virginia was still, on paper, where he lived.

**What the timing shows.** The case was filed **April 5, 2018** — the day after
[[wiki/people/fran-coldren|Fran]] died on April 4. The summons was printed at
2:51 PM that afternoon and addressed to 337 Saratoga Drive. It would have
arrived in the mail during the week of her funeral. Nothing in any telling of
this story mentions the envelope; the two videos of the sheet, shot ten minutes
apart on **April 17**, are the only trace that it landed at all, and the fact
that he filmed it twice is the closest thing to a reaction the record holds.

Alongside the 2015 retail theft ([[wiki/legal/2015-retail-theft-arrest]]) it is
the second time a want of essentially zero value ran all the way to official
paperwork — and now the second time that paperwork has a docket number attached
to it. Both were filed in the same magisterial district, before the same judge,
three years apart: [[wiki/legal/2015-possession-arrest]] records Michael Metros
from the February 2015 court blotter and states that he "appears once ... and
has no other trace in the corpus." He appears twice. MDJ-14-1-01 is the constant
in Dan's charging record; the offences have nothing else in common.

## Dating

The captures place this in April, during the pediatric-wing phase and after
the water was stopped, which brackets it between the **April 1, 2018**
admission and the **April 4, 2018** death. The summons now supplies a hard
outer bound the captures could not: the case was **filed April 5, 2018**, so the
incident cannot be later than that. It does not supply the offence date — no
offence-date field is legible in the surviving frames — so the range is narrowed
at the top rather than fixed. The one detail that would tighten it further, the
capture's "day four of the water shutdown," which the vigil page also carries,
points at April 3 or 4; a citation written by a security guard on the 3rd or 4th
and docketed by the magistrate on the next business day is exactly what an
April 5 filing looks like, and that is corroboration of the derived date rather
than proof of it. The captures' own year, 2017, is corrected to 2018 on the same
evidence set out at [[wiki/timeline/events/the-fall-of-fran]] — and now
independently, by a printed court document reading **2018**.

## Gaps

**The disposition is the live question now.** The summons closes the "was
anything filed" gap and opens a sharper one: what happened to docket
MJ-14101-NT-0000082-2018. Both plea lines are unsigned in the last image anyone
has of the sheet. The fine and costs are printed on it but not legible at this
resolution, so even the amount at stake is unknown. Pennsylvania's UJS web
portal — named on the summons itself — carries summary-case dockets and would
answer plea, disposition, amount and payment history in one lookup; nobody has
run it. Failing that, the operator's own memory of whether he paid, appeared, or
ignored it is a T0 source that has never been asked for.

The **video the frames come from** is not on disk — only three screenshots of it
playing in Photos. Two clips exist (4:31 PM and 4:41 PM on April 17); recovering
them would likely resolve the fine and costs row and the barcode block, and the
4:31 clip may pan across fields these frames cut off, the offence date among
them.

The reading of the charge as a **Uniontown local ordinance** rests on `LO` being
the MDJS charge-type prefix for one, which is convention rather than anything
printed on the sheet. The ordinance's text — what conduct no. 1639 (b)(1)
actually reaches, and whether it names vaporizers or only combustion — is
outside the corpus, and it is the document that would say whether Dan's
combustion argument had any legal purchase at all.

The hospital's own record — an incident report, a trespass notice — is still
unsought and is now the only thing that would establish whether Dan was
permitted back onto the property before Fran died, which matters because
[[wiki/people/diane-moore|Diane]]'s letter had already excluded him from the
shift rotation; the two exclusions may have overlapped without either being the
operative one. Annie's reaction, once she learned what had happened, is not
recorded anywhere, and neither is anyone else's reaction to the envelope
arriving during the week of the funeral.
